summary: A plain document has the witnesses sign on the inside, and a folded, tied document has them sign on the back. If they signed in the wrong place it is not valid, though Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says it all follows the local custom.

chunks.en: A plain document:
chunks.st: In an ordinary document,

chunks.en: its witnesses sign on the inside.
chunks.st: its witnesses are to sign inside it, i.e., on the written side of the paper.

chunks.en: And a tied document: its witnesses sign on the back.
chunks.st: In a folded and tied document, its witnesses are to sign on the back of it.

words.note: Folded and sewn closed, with witnesses signing on each fold.

chunks.en: A plain one whose witnesses signed on the back,
chunks.st: With regard to an ordinary document whose witnesses wrote their signatures on the back of it,

chunks.en: and a tied one whose witnesses signed on the inside:
chunks.st: and a tied document whose witnesses wrote their signatures inside of it,

chunks.en: both are not valid.
chunks.st: both of these are not valid.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: A tied one whose witnesses signed on the inside
chunks.st: A tied document whose witnesses wrote their signatures inside of it

chunks.en: is valid, because he can make it into a plain one.
chunks.st: is valid, because one can transform it into an ordinary document by untying it.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: It all follows the custom of the place.
chunks.st: Everything is in accordance with regional custom.

summary: A plain document needs two witnesses and a tied one needs three. If the amount written in a document is unclear or rubbed out, the lender gets only the smaller amount, and if the top and bottom amounts are different, we follow the bottom one.

chunks.en: A plain document has two witnesses,
chunks.st: An ordinary document is rendered valid by its having at least two witnesses,

chunks.en: and a tied one, three.
chunks.st: and a tied document is rendered valid by its having at least three witnesses.

chunks.en: A plain one with one witness signed on it,
chunks.st: With regard to an ordinary document in which a single witness wrote his signature,

chunks.en: and a tied one with two witnesses signed on it:
chunks.st: and a tied document in which only two witnesses wrote their signatures,

chunks.en: both are not valid.
chunks.st: they are both not valid.

chunks.en: If he wrote in it: A hundred zuz
chunks.st: If it is written in a document that someone owes: One hundred dinars,

chunks.en: which are twenty sela,
chunks.st: which are twenty sela,
chunks.stMore: which is internally inconsistent since there are twenty-five sela in a hundred dinars,

words.note: A sela is a coin worth four zuz.

chunks.en: he gets only twenty.
chunks.st: the holder of the document has the right to claim only twenty sela, the lower of the two amounts.

chunks.en: A hundred zuz which are thirty sela:
chunks.st: If it is written that he owes: One hundred dinars, which are thirty sela,

chunks.en: he gets only a maneh.
chunks.st: the holder of the document has the right to claim only one hundred dinars, again the lower of the two amounts.

chunks.en: Silver zuz that are...
chunks.st: If it is written that someone owes: Silver dinars that are,

chunks.en: and the rest was rubbed out: not less than two.
chunks.st: and the remainder of the text, where the number of dinars should be specified, was erased, the amount must be no less than two
chunks.stMore: dinars, the lowest amount to which the plural word dinars can be referring. That is what the creditor can claim.

chunks.en: Silver sela that are...
chunks.st: Similarly, if it is written: Silver sela that are,

chunks.en: and the rest was rubbed out: not less than two.
chunks.st: and the remainder of the text was erased, the amount must be no less than two sela.

chunks.en: Darics that are...
chunks.st: And if it is written: Darics that are,

chunks.en: and the rest was rubbed out: not less than two.
chunks.st: and the remainder of the text was erased, the amount must be no less than two darics.

chunks.he: כָּתוּב בּוֹ מִלְמַעְלָה מָנֶה וּמִלְּמַטָּה מָאתַיִם,
chunks.en: If it says a maneh at the top and two hundred at the bottom,
chunks.st: If it is written in the document above, in an earlier place in the document, that someone owes one hundred dinars, and below, toward the end of the document, it is written that the amount owed is two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: or two hundred at the top and a maneh at the bottom,
chunks.st: or if above it is written two hundred dinars and below one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: everything follows the bottom one.
chunks.st: everything follows the bottom amount.

chunks.he: אִם כֵּן, לָמָּה כוֹתְבִין אֶת הָעֶלְיוֹן,
chunks.en: If so, why do we write the top one?
chunks.st: If so, why does one write the information in the upper part of the document at all?

chunks.he: שֶׁאִם תִּמָּחֵק אוֹת אַחַת מִן הַתַּחְתּוֹן,
chunks.en: So that if one letter is rubbed out from the bottom one,
chunks.st: It is a safety measure, so that if one letter is erased from the lower
chunks.stMore: part of the document, thereby rendering it illegible,

chunks.en: we can learn it from the top one.
chunks.st: the information can be learned from the upper part of the document.

summary: A scribe may write some documents for one person without the other being there, like a get for a husband or a loan paper for a borrower. For a lender or a buyer, the other side must be there too, and the person whom the paper helps pays the scribe.

chunks.en: We may write a get for a man
chunks.st: A scribe may write a bill of divorce for a man who requests one,

words.note: A paper a husband gives his wife to end the marriage.

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין אִשְׁתּוֹ עִמּוֹ,
chunks.en: even if his wife is not with him,
chunks.st: even if his wife is not with him
chunks.stMore: to give her consent when he presents his request, as there is no possibility that he will misuse the document.

chunks.en: and a receipt for a woman
chunks.st: And a scribe may write a receipt for a woman
chunks.stMore: upon her request, attesting to the payment of her marriage contract,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בַּעְלָהּ עִמָּהּ,
chunks.en: even if her husband is not with her,
chunks.st: even if her husband is not with her to give his consent.

chunks.en: as long as the scribe knows them,
chunks.st: This is true provided that the scribe recognizes
chunks.stMore: the parties requesting the document, to prevent misrepresentation.

chunks.en: and the husband pays the scribe.
chunks.st: And for both documents, the husband gives the scribe his wages.

chunks.en: We may write a loan paper for a borrower
chunks.st: A scribe may write a promissory note for a debtor who requests one,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מַלְוֶה עִמּוֹ,
chunks.en: even if the lender is not with him,
chunks.st: even if the creditor is not with him when he requests the document,

chunks.en: but we may not write one for a lender
chunks.st: but a scribe may not write a promissory note for a creditor who requests it

chunks.en: unless the borrower is with him,
chunks.st: unless the debtor is with him and consents.

chunks.en: and the borrower pays the scribe.
chunks.st: And it is the debtor who gives the scribe his wages.

chunks.en: We may write a sale paper for a seller
chunks.st: A scribe may write a bill of sale for a seller of a field who requests one

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹקֵחַ עִמּוֹ.
chunks.en: even if the buyer is not with him,
chunks.st: even if the purchaser is not with him when he presents his request,

chunks.en: but we may not write one for a buyer
chunks.st: but a scribe may not write a bill of sale for a purchaser who requests it

chunks.en: unless the seller is with him,
chunks.st: unless the seller is with him and consents.

chunks.en: and the buyer pays the scribe.
chunks.st: And it is the purchaser who gives the scribe his wages.

summary: Some papers, like a wedding contract, a farming deal, or a court agreement, may be written only when both sides agree. The mishnah says who pays the scribe, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says each side gets its own copy.

chunks.en: We do not write papers for kiddushin and marriage
chunks.st: A scribe may not write documents of betrothal and documents of marriage

words.note: When a man and woman become engaged to be married.

chunks.en: unless both of them agree,
chunks.st: except with the consent of both parties, the groom and the bride.

chunks.en: and the groom pays the scribe.
chunks.st: And it is the groom who gives the scribe his wages.

chunks.en: We do not write papers for sharecropping and building jobs
chunks.st: A scribe may not write contracts for sharecroppers and contractors

chunks.en: unless both of them agree,
chunks.st: except with the consent of both
chunks.stMore: parties, i.e., the sharecropper or contractor and the one who hires him.

chunks.en: and the one who takes the job pays the scribe.
chunks.st: And it is the sharecropper or contractor who gives the scribe his wages.

words.en: and the one who takes the job

chunks.en: We do not write papers of choosing judges
chunks.st: A scribe may not write documents testifying to arbitration agreements

chunks.en: or any other court paper
chunks.st: or any other court enactment

chunks.en: unless both of them agree,
chunks.st: except with the consent of both parties to the litigation.

chunks.en: and both of them pay the scribe.
chunks.st: And both parties give the scribe his wages.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: For the two of them he writes two copies,
chunks.st: The scribe writes two documents for the two parties,

chunks.en: one for this one himself, and one for that one himself.
chunks.st: one for this one by himself, and one for that one by himself.

summary: A borrower paid back part of his loan, and the loan paper was given to a third person. The borrower said that if he does not pay the rest by a certain day, the paper should be given to the lender, and Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yehuda argue whether it is.

chunks.en: Someone who paid part of his debt
chunks.st: In the case of a debtor who repaid part of his debt and

chunks.en: and gave his loan paper to a third person,
chunks.st: with the agreement of the creditor deposited the promissory note with a third party
chunks.stMore: serving as a trustee to ensure that the creditor would not collect the full amount,

words.en: and gave to a third person

chunks.en: and said to him,
chunks.st: and the debtor said to the trustee:

chunks.en: If I do not give you
chunks.st: If I have not given you the balance

chunks.en: from now until such-and-such a day,
chunks.st: from now until such and such a day,

chunks.en: give him his paper.
chunks.explain: Then the lender can collect the whole loan.
chunks.st: give the creditor his promissory note,
chunks.stMore: thereby enabling him to collect the full amount stated on the note,

chunks.en: The time came and he did not give it:
chunks.st: if the stipulated time arrived and the debtor did not give the balance to the trustee,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says: He should give it.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says: The trustee should give
chunks.stMore: the promissory note to the creditor, in accordance with the debtor’s stipulation.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: He should not give it.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: The trustee should not give it, as the stipulation is void.

summary: If a loan paper was rubbed out, witnesses who remember it come to beis din, which writes a new paper in its place. If a borrower paid back part of a loan, Rabbi Yehuda says to write a new loan paper, and Rabbi Yosei says to write a receipt.

chunks.en: Someone whose loan paper was rubbed out
chunks.st: In the case of a creditor whose promissory note has become erased,

chunks.en: brings witnesses about it,
chunks.st: he should produce witnesses who remember the details of the document to testify about it.

chunks.en: and comes before beis din,
chunks.st: And they come before the court,

chunks.en: and they make a new proof for him:
chunks.st: and they ratify his promissory note for him,

chunks.en: So-and-so son of so-and-so
chunks.st: stating: The promissory note of so-and-so

chunks.en: had his paper rubbed out on such-and-such a day,
chunks.st: was erased, and it stated that a loan for such and such an amount took place on such and such a date,

chunks.en: and these two people were its witnesses.
chunks.st: and so-and-so and so-and-so were its witnesses.
chunks.stMore: The ratification document is signed, and it may be used as a replacement for the erased document.

chunks.en: Someone who paid back part of his debt:
chunks.st: In the case of a debtor who repaid part of his debt,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: He changes the paper for a new one.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: The creditor should exchange
chunks.stMore: the promissory note for a new one stating the current balance and tear up the first promissory note.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says: He writes a receipt.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says: The creditor may keep the original promissory note, and he should write a receipt
chunks.stMore: for the payment he has received and give it to the debtor as proof of his partial payment of the sum recorded in the old note.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said with regard to this arrangement:

chunks.he: נִמְצָא זֶה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת שׁוֹמֵר שׁוֹבְרוֹ
chunks.en: Then the borrower must guard his receipt
chunks.st: It is found that this debtor must now guard his receipt

chunks.en: from the mice!
chunks.st: against being destroyed by mice,
chunks.stMore: as if he no longer has the receipt, he will have to pay the entire sum recorded in the promissory note.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said to him:

chunks.en: That is good for him,
chunks.st: This situation is fitting for him; it is better that this procedure be followed,

chunks.en: so that the lender's power is not made weaker.
chunks.st: and the strength of the claim of this creditor not be weakened.

summary: This mishnah teaches many money rules: brothers who share a bathhouse, two men with the same name, unclear loan papers, and when a lender may collect from a guarantor. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel also teaches how to stop a trick with a kesubah guarantor.

chunks.he: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד עָנִי וְאֶחָד עָשִׁיר,
chunks.en: Two brothers, one poor and one rich,
chunks.st: In a case where there are two brothers, one poor and one rich,

chunks.he: וְהִנִּיחַ לָהֶן אֲבִיהֶן מֶרְחָץ וּבֵית הַבַּד,
chunks.en: and their father left them a bathhouse and an olive press:
chunks.st: and their father left them a bathhouse or an olive press as an inheritance,

chunks.en: if he made them to earn money, the money is shared.
chunks.st: if the father had built these facilities for profit, i.e., to charge others for using them, the profit that accrues after the father’s death is shared equally by the two brothers.

chunks.en: If he made them for himself,
chunks.st: If the father had built them for himself
chunks.stMore: and for the members of his household to use, the poor brother, who has little use for these amenities, cannot force the rich brother to convert the facilities to commercial use; rather,

chunks.en: the rich brother can say to the poor one,
chunks.st: the rich brother can say to the poor brother: Go

chunks.en: Take yourself servants and let them wash in the bathhouse.
chunks.st: take servants for yourself, and they will bathe in the bathhouse.

chunks.en: Take yourself olives
chunks.st: Or he can say: Go take olives for yourself,

chunks.en: and come and make them into oil in the olive press.
chunks.st: and come and make them into oil in the olive press.

chunks.en: Two people who lived in one city,
chunks.st: If there are two people who were living in one city,

chunks.en: one named Yosef ben Shimon
chunks.st: one named Yosef ben Shimon

chunks.en: and the other named Yosef ben Shimon:
chunks.st: and the other also named Yosef ben Shimon,

chunks.en: they cannot bring a loan paper
chunks.st: one cannot present a promissory note

chunks.en: against each other,
chunks.st: against the other,
chunks.stMore: as the purported debtor can claim: On the contrary, it is you who owed me money; you repaid me and I returned this note to you upon payment.

chunks.he: וְלֹא אַחֵר יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיא עֲלֵיהֶן שְׁטָר חוֹב.
chunks.en: and no one else can bring a loan paper against them.
chunks.st: Nor can another, third person, present a promissory note against either of them,
chunks.stMore: as each one can claim: It is not I but the other Yosef ben Shimon who owes you money.

chunks.en: If someone found among his papers
chunks.st: If a document is found among one’s documents

chunks.he: שְׁטָרוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן פָּרוּעַ,
chunks.en: The paper of Yosef ben Shimon is paid,
chunks.st: stating: The promissory note against Yosef ben Shimon is repaid,
chunks.stMore: and both men named Yosef ben Shimon owed this man money,

chunks.en: then both of their papers are paid.
chunks.st: the promissory notes of both of them are considered repaid,
chunks.stMore: as it cannot be determined which debt was repaid and which is outstanding.

chunks.en: What should they do? They should write three names.
chunks.explain: Yosef son of Shimon son of his grandfather.
chunks.st: What should two people with the same name in a single city do in order to conduct their business? They should triple
chunks.stMore: their names by writing three generations: Yosef ben Shimon ben so-and-so.

chunks.en: And if those were the same too, they write a sign.
chunks.st: And if they have identical triple names, i.e., not only their fathers but their grandfathers had identical names, they should write an indication
chunks.stMore: as to which one is referred to, such as: The short Yosef ben Shimon or the dark Yosef ben Shimon.

chunks.en: And if the signs were the same, they write Kohen.
chunks.st: And if they have identical indications, they should write: Yosef ben Shimon the priest, if one of them is a priest.

chunks.en: Someone who says to his son,
chunks.st: In the case of one who says to his son

chunks.en: One paper among my papers is paid,
chunks.st: before dying: One promissory note among the promissory notes in my possession is repaid,

chunks.en: and I do not know which one:
chunks.st: but I do not know which one,

chunks.en: then all the papers are paid.
chunks.st: the promissory notes of all of those who owe him money are considered repaid,
chunks.stMore: i.e., they are not valid for collection, as it cannot be determined which debt was repaid and which are outstanding.

chunks.en: If two were found from one person,
chunks.st: If there were found among his papers two promissory notes owed by one person,

chunks.en: the bigger one is paid and the smaller one is not paid.
chunks.st: the one for the greater amount is considered repaid, and the one for the smaller amount is not considered repaid
chunks.stMore: and can be collected; the debtor is favored in the case of an uncertainty.

chunks.he: הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ עַל יְדֵי עָרֵב,
chunks.en: Someone who lends his friend with a guarantor
chunks.st: One who lends money to another with the assurance of a guarantor

words.note: A person who promises to pay if the borrower does not.

chunks.en: may not collect from the guarantor.
chunks.st: cannot collect the debt from the guarantor.

chunks.en: But if he said,
chunks.st: But if the creditor said to the debtor:

chunks.en: On the condition that I collect from whoever I want,
chunks.st: I am lending the money on the condition that I will collect the debt from whomever I wish, i.e., either the debtor or the guarantor,

chunks.en: he may collect from the guarantor.
chunks.st: he can collect the debt from the guarantor.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: If the borrower has property,
chunks.st: If the debtor has property of his own,

chunks.en: either way
chunks.st: then whether in this case, where the creditor stipulated this condition, or that case, where he did not,

chunks.en: he may not collect from the guarantor.
chunks.st: he cannot collect the debt from the guarantor.

chunks.he: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר,
chunks.en: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel also used to say:
chunks.st: And so Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel would say:

chunks.he: הֶעָרֵב לָאִשָּׁה בִּכְתֻבָּתָהּ וְהָיָה בַעְלָהּ מְגָרְשָׁהּ,
chunks.en: Someone who is the guarantor for a woman's kesubah, and her husband was divorcing her:
chunks.st: If there is a guarantor for a woman for her marriage contract, from whom the woman can collect payment of her marriage contract instead of collecting it from the husband, and her husband was divorcing her,

chunks.en: he must make a neder never to benefit from her,
chunks.st: the husband must take a vow prohibiting himself from deriving any benefit from her, so that he can never remarry her.

words.en: he must make her forbidden by a neder

chunks.en: in case they make a trick
chunks.st: This precaution is taken lest the couple collude [kenunya]
chunks.stMore: to divorce in order to collect payment of the marriage contract

chunks.en: to get the guarantor's property,
chunks.st: from this guarantor’s property,

chunks.en: and then he takes his wife back.
chunks.st: and then the husband will remarry his wife.

summary: A lender with a signed loan paper can even collect from land the borrower later sold, but with only witnesses or a handwritten note he collects only from what the borrower still has. Ben Nanas teaches when a guarantor must pay, and Rabbi Yishmael praises learning money laws.

chunks.en: Someone who lends his friend with a document
chunks.st: One who lends money to another by means of a promissory note

chunks.en: collects even from property that was sold.
chunks.st: can collect the debt from liened property
chunks.stMore: that had been sold to others by the debtor after the loan was granted.

words.note: Property that was sold after the loan, which the loan still holds onto.

chunks.en: With only witnesses,
chunks.st: One who lends money by means of witnesses,
chunks.stMore: without recording the loan in a promissory note,

chunks.en: he collects only from property the borrower still has.
chunks.st: can collect the debt only from unsold property.

chunks.en: If he brought out the borrower's handwriting
chunks.st: If one presents to a debtor a document in the handwriting of the debtor stating

chunks.en: that says he owes him,
chunks.st: that he owes money to him, but without witnesses signed on the document,

chunks.en: he collects only from property the borrower still has.
chunks.st: the creditor can collect only from unsold property.

chunks.en: A guarantor who signed after the witnesses signed the loan paper:
chunks.st: In the case of a guarantor whose commitment emerged after the signing of the promissory note,

chunks.en: he collects only from property he still has.
chunks.st: the creditor can collect the sum only from unsold property of the guarantor.

chunks.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בָא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְאָמַר,
chunks.en: A case came before Rabbi Yishmael, and he said,
chunks.st: The mishna relates: An incident occurred where such a case came before Rabbi Yishmael, and he said:

chunks.en: he collects from property he still has.
chunks.st: The creditor can collect the sum from unsold property
chunks.stMore: of the guarantor, but not from liened property that he has sold to others.

chunks.en: Ben Nanas said to him,
chunks.st: Ben Nannas said to Rabbi Yishmael:

chunks.en: he does not collect, not from sold property
chunks.st: The creditor cannot collect the sum from the guarantor at all, not from liened property that has been sold,

chunks.en: and not from property he still has.
chunks.st: nor from unsold property.

chunks.en: He said to him, Why?
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael said to him: Why not?

chunks.en: He said to him:
chunks.st: Ben Nannas said to him:

chunks.en: If someone was grabbing a person in the market to make him pay,
chunks.st: If one was strangling someone in the marketplace, demanding repayment of a loan,

chunks.he: וּמְצָאוֹ חֲבֵרוֹ וְאָמַר לוֹ הַנַּח לוֹ,
chunks.en: and his friend found him and said, Leave him alone,
chunks.st: and another person found him doing so and said to the attacker: Leave him alone and I will give you the money he owes,

chunks.en: he does not have to pay, because the loan was not made trusting him.
chunks.st: the person who intervened is exempt from paying, as the creditor did not loan the money in the first place based on his trust of the one who intervened.

chunks.en: So which guarantor does have to pay?
chunks.st: Rather, who is a guarantor who is obligated to repay the loan he has guaranteed?

chunks.en: One who says, Lend him and I will pay you,
chunks.st: One who tells the creditor before the loan takes place: Lend money to him, and I will give you the repayment,

chunks.en: he must pay, because the loan was made trusting him.
chunks.st: as in that case the creditor did loan the money based on his trust of the guarantor.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael said:
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yishmael thereupon said:

chunks.en: Whoever wants to become wise
chunks.st: One who wants to become wise

chunks.en: should learn the laws of money,
chunks.st: should engage in the study of monetary law,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ מִקְצוֹעַ בַּתּוֹרָה גָּדוֹל מֵהֶן,
chunks.en: because there is no part of the Torah greater than them,
chunks.st: as there is no greater discipline in the Torah,

chunks.en: for they are like a flowing spring.
chunks.st: and it is like a flowing spring.

chunks.en: And whoever wants to learn the laws of money
chunks.st: And, he added, one who wants to engage in the study of monetary law

chunks.en: should serve and learn from Shimon ben Nanas.
chunks.st: should attend to, i.e., become a disciple of, Shimon ben Nannas.
